BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller package.** The preamble, "[STANDARD]" tags and "Reviewer Efficiency Note" assert that positions are "market standard", "settled at principal level", "FINAL" and "pre-cleared by both sides". None of this is confirmed through our authority process (playbook §0.4/6.3), and our playbook records no Amelia Frost approval of any fallback. Every clause has therefore been reviewed in full; the Seller's labelling has been disregarded. I also note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (§11) contradicts the cover email: it expressly states that no negotiation position or approval is included.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- *Buyer wants:* 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure coincides with our conditional fallback, but no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft exists, so the fallback is not available.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- *Buyer wants:* De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure would forfeit the first AUD 250,000 of every valid claim.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; and all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded (cl 12.3/13).
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months for general Warranty Claims; limitations apply only to the claim categories they are drafted for.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the catch-all language is a hidden general-regime override (see N-014).

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- *Buyer wants:* Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six-year period, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject outright.** A 20%/18-month limit on title would leave the Buyer unable to recover the price if it does not get the shares; "administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* No carve-out; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature".
- *Buyer wants:* Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; insert express carve-out.** This is a non-waivable playbook position and the Seller's blanket drafting would purport to cap or exclude liability for fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL §1.1–1.2).
- *Buyer wants:* Specific fair disclosure only – facts disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; replace with a fair-disclosure standard tied to the Disclosure Letter.** General data-room disclosure would hollow out the warranties and the Seller's own DL §11 confirms the Buyer must evaluate the facts itself, which only works if disclosure is specific.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- *Buyer wants:* Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer deal persons; Seller-knowledge qualifiers in warranties must reference named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject.** "Discoverable" plus adviser knowledge effectively re-imports general disclosure and would bar claims on matters the Buyer never actually knew of.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL §2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- *Buyer wants:* Condition precedent requiring effective consent AND evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; stronger than reasonable endeavours for a customer representing ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject.** Consent-on-delivery ignores the conditions in cl 11.3, and reasonable endeavours is insufficient protection for a material customer whose consent is currently absent.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL §3 confirms not repaid, no discharge.
- *Buyer wants:* Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject.** The deal is debt-free/cash-free; completing with AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding and only a promise of future release exposes the Buyer to the lender's change-of-control rights (cl 8.1) and unreleased security.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL §5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- *Buyer wants:* Bonuses plus all triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item funded by the Seller (or deducted from price), with a Seller warranty/indemnity as to quantum.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; require express line item and Seller funding.** Bonuses triggered by Completion and payable by the Company will otherwise become a Buyer cost by default, and the on-cost exposure is unquantified.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL §4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Broadened indemnity covering failure of title to SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims and remediation costs, while preserving the cure mechanism (pay SOW3 fees → materials transfer); plus delivery of a confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject as drafted; broaden.** The core risk is IP title, not just a payment, and the AUD 180,000 remains unverified in either direction so the indemnity cannot be sized to that number.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL §6: ~1,240 records; access, scope and notification duty undetermined; no confirmed breach; no loss figure.
- *Buyer wants:* Covenant to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation, provide pre-Completion updates and a bring-down; specific indemnity for notification/regulatory/third-party costs if a breach is later established. Do not assume a breach or harm, and do not accept a numeric exposure either way.
- *Recommendation:* **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation; add investigation/update covenant and conditional indemnity.** The facts are genuinely open, so the right response is process and allocation, not a conclusion.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- *Seller:* Ordinary-course operating costs. DL §8: three renewals of AUD 110,000 (DD-008/DD-011); no statement on whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- *Buyer wants:* Further diligence (timing, termination rights, whether already accrued/invoiced) before classification; no automatic Debt or price adjustment, but reserve the position pending answers.
- *Recommendation:* **Hold open; request information.** Neither the Seller's "ordinary course" label nor a Debt classification is supported yet.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* Cl 13 default that limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to all Claims; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Separate, expressly drafted regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants; general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject.** The Seller's drafting is a hidden general-regime override that would collapse every protection into the 20%/18-month box.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL §10 concedes this is the Seller-supplied source and the Buyer has not verified.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical searches, PPSR search, constitution, board/shareholder resolutions, review of share certificates and transfer chain, capacity/authority evidence for Harbourglass, and encumbrance/charge searches, with title warranties under the Fundamental regime.
- *Recommendation:* **Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient; commission independent verification.** An internal register is a Seller-controlled document and the Seller itself declines to say it has been verified.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP warranty positions "settled" under the general regime.
- *Buyer wants:* Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate regimes to be negotiated (tax typically with a longer limitation period aligned to assessment windows and a tax indemnity; IP with ownership warranties linked to the Ironquay position). No assumption of unlimited liability and no assumption of resolution.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the "settled" assertion; mark as OPEN.** Nothing has been agreed on Tax or IP and the Seller's statement is an attempt to fold them into the general cap by assertion.

---

**Summary for the deal team**
- 15 of 16 issues: Seller position rejected or not accepted as drafted; 1 (Sandbar) held open for information.
- No fallback has been triggered. The 20% cap and 18-month period both require Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying this draft, which does not exist; if the team wishes to consider them, that approval must be obtained first – it should not be inferred from the Seller's "FINAL"/"agreed" labelling.
- Recommended cover response to Seller: we do not accept that any clause is cleared, agreed or final; full mark-up to follow on the above basis.
